import type { ReactNode } from 'react' import { Button as AriaButton } from 'react-aria-components' import type { ButtonProps as AriaButtonProps } from 'react-aria-components' export interface ButtonIconProps { /** * The icon markup, typically an inline `svg]:block [&>svg]:shrink-0', // The default, and only for an icon that did not name its own size — see the note above. '[&>svg:not([class*=size-])]:h-[1cap]', '[&>svg:not([class*=size-])]:w-auto', ].join(' ')} > {children} ) } /** * Layout slot for a `Button` label. Use it as `Button.Text`. Truncates rather * than wrapping so a long label cannot change the control's height. * * Exported as `ButtonText` only so tooling can resolve it; consume the * compound form `Button.Text`. */ export function ButtonText({ children }: ButtonTextProps) { return ( {children} ) } /** * The indeterminate indicator shown while `isPending`. Hand-rolled rather than * React Aria's `ProgressBar`, which renders a `
` — not phrasing content, * so it cannot legally sit inside a `

/**
 * The sheet's `.ds-select-menu`, shared by everything that opens over the page: `Menu` now, and
 * `Select` and `ComboBox` when they converge onto it. The same split as `field.ts` — the surface is
 * the thing that must not drift, and the slots are still defined per component so Storybook
 * documents them under the right name.
 *
 * The shadow is the one literal colour in this file: it is a **shadow**, not a surface, and every
 * attempt to derive one from a token produces a haze rather than a shadow. It is `rgba(0,0,0,.7)`
 * because a shadow has to darken in both themes, exactly as the modal's scrim does.
 */
export const SURFACE = [
  'border border-border-strong bg-card rounded-xl',
  'shadow-[0_12px_32px_rgba(0,0,0,.7)]',
  // **A transparent outline at rest, never `outline-none`.** The property is shared —
  // `outline-none` writes `--tw-outline-style`, which every `outline-<width>` reads
  // back — so a ring written beside it can never draw. `Popover` is the part here that
  // takes real focus (a popover with no focusable child is focusable itself).
  'outline-1 -outline-offset-2 outline-transparent',
].join(' ')

/**
 * A popover that holds a single scrolling list: **at least as wide as the control it came from, and
 * wider when an option needs it.**
 *
 * `min-w`, not `w`. A trigger is sized for its own label — a `Select` says "Frankfurt", a `Menu` button
 * says "Actions" — and a panel sized to exactly that cuts off the one option longer than the control,
 * which is usually the option the reader opened the menu to find. Growing to fit the content is what a
 * native popup does, and `w-(--trigger-width)` was the only rule here that could not.
 *
 * The `max-w` is the guard that growth needs: it is the window minus the same 1rem gutter the modal's
 * overlay keeps, so a label long enough to run off the page truncates instead. `min-width` outranks
 * `max-width` in CSS, so a trigger already wider than that cap (a full-width field on a phone) still
 * gets its own width and is never squashed. React Aria writes `--trigger-width` as an inline custom
 * property and no width of its own, so this class is what decides.
 */
export const POPOVER = `flex min-w-(--trigger-width) max-w-[calc(100vw-2rem)] flex-col overflow-clip ${SURFACE}`

/** The list inside it. `max-h` so a long list scrolls rather than running off the page. */
export const LIST =
  'max-h-[264px] overflow-auto overscroll-contain p-0 outline-none'

/**
 * The sheet's `.ds-select-option`: 13px at 75%, with the accent reserved for the choice.
 *
 * Hover and focus land on the same treatment on purpose. A menu is walked with the arrow keys as
 * much as with a pointer, so the row the keyboard has reached and the row the pointer is over
 * should not look like two different kinds of thing.
 */
export const ITEM = [
  'relative flex items-center justify-between gap-3',
  'px-3.5 py-[11px] text-[13px] text-foreground/75',
  'cursor-pointer select-none',
  'data-[hovered]:bg-foreground/7 data-[hovered]:text-foreground',
  'data-[pressed]:bg-foreground/12',
  'data-[focus-visible]:outline-none data-[focus-visible]:bg-foreground/7 data-[focus-visible]:text-foreground',
  'data-[selected]:text-primary',
  'data-[disabled]:cursor-not-allowed data-[disabled]:text-foreground/35',
].join(' ')

/** One item's text, which truncates rather than wrapping a menu wider than its trigger. */
export const ITEM_LABEL = 'truncate'

/** A run of items, announced as a group. */
export const SECTION = 'flex flex-col'

/** The sheet's `.ds-select-group-label`. */
export const SECTION_TITLE = [
  'px-3.5 pt-[9px] pb-1',
  'text-[11px] uppercase tracking-[0.08em] text-foreground/45',
].join(' ')

/** The sheet's `.ds-div-hair`, inset so it reads as a break in the list rather than a table edge. */
export const SEPARATOR = 'my-1 h-px shrink-0 bg-border'

/** A search box above the list sits behind the menu's own hairline, so it reads as part of the surface. */
export const SEARCH = 'border-b border-border-strong p-2'

/**
 * A submenu's caret. A row with a submenu says so — `data-has-submenu` is React Aria's — and an
 * affordance nobody can see is not an affordance.
 */
export const SUBMENU_CARET = [
  'shrink-0 text-foreground/45',
  'motion-safe:transition-[rotate] motion-safe:duration-(--duration-fast) ease-pulse',
  'data-[open]:rotate-90',
].join(' ')

docs:
A panel that slides in from an edge — a task's details without leaving the page.

```tsx
<Sheet>
  <Button>Details</Button>
  <Sheet.Content side="right">
    <Sheet.Title>fra1 · Frankfurt</Sheet.Title>
    <Sheet.Description>Checked every 60 seconds.</Sheet.Description>
    <Sheet.Footer>
      <Sheet.Close>Close</Sheet.Close>
    </Sheet.Footer>
  </Sheet.Content>
</Sheet>
```

| Slot                | React Aria                                | Notes                                           |
| ------------------- | ----------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `Sheet`             | `DialogTrigger`                           | The trigger, then a `Sheet.Content`             |
| `Sheet.Content`     | `SheetOverlay` + `Sheet` + `SheetContent` | The scrim, the edge, and the panel              |
| `Sheet.Title`       | `Heading`                                 | The modal's own title type, imported not copied |
| `Sheet.Description` | `Text`                                    | `aria-describedby` wired here, as on `Modal`    |
| `Sheet.Footer`      | —                                         | The actions, pushed to the foot                 |
| `Sheet.Close`       | `Button`                                  | `slot="close"`, the whole mechanism             |

**A sheet is a modal that kept the page visible.** It takes the pointer and traps focus exactly as a
`Modal` does, but covers one edge instead of the middle — so the row you opened it from is still on
screen behind the scrim. Reach for `Modal` when the page is irrelevant to the decision and for this
when it is the context.

It is also a **swipe target on touch**, which is why `side` is not merely a layout prop: React Aria
resolves it into the edge _and_ the swipe direction, so a right-hand panel is dismissed by dragging
right.

## Three layers, and none of them is optional

`SheetOverlay` owns the state and draws the scrim, `Sheet` reads that state and decides the edge, and
`SheetContent` reads _its_ result. Content placed straight inside `Sheet` leaves `SheetContext` null:
`Cannot destructure property 'position' of useContext(...)` — which reads like a React bug and is a
missing layer.

**`position` is a `SheetOverlay` prop** — not `Sheet`, not `SheetContent`.

## The panel cannot be sized from outside — size the layer above it

`SheetContent` renders a `Dialog` with `style={{ width: '100%', height: '100%' }}` written _after_ the
props it is given. **An inline style outranks every class**, so a `w-96` passed to the panel does
nothing at all, and the panel is always exactly as big as the layer above it.

The size therefore goes on `Sheet`, which this component owns — `SIZES[side]` in JavaScript, where
`side` is already known. The first version put it on the panel and rendered a **250×149** panel while
the class list looked perfectly correct.

### The panel scrolls, now that it has to

The panel cannot be sized from outside (above), so it is exactly as tall as its layer — and for one
round it also had no overflow of its own. A sheet whose content ran past the viewport therefore had no
scrollbar anywhere, `mbs-auto` on the footer had no free space to claim, and the content below the fold
was simply unreachable. `SheetContent` now carries `min-h-0 overflow-y-auto overscroll-contain`, and the
edge-anchored sheets inset themselves from the home indicator and the notch
(`env(safe-area-inset-*)` on `SIZES.bottom` and `SIZES.top`), which needs
`viewport-fit=cover` in the root route's viewport meta — without it every inset is `0px`.

## The two earlier verdicts, revisited

This component was built, removed, and rebuilt. Both reasons it was removed are worth recording as
they turned out:

- **"It opens on load" was wrong.** A throwaway Playwright probe that navigates straight to an
  `iframe.html?viewMode=story` URL reports a dialog already open for _every_ overlay story here,
  because Storybook restores that story's canvas from a previous visit in the same browser context.
  The runner asserts the opposite: `Default`'s **first** assertion is that no dialog is present, made
  before any click, and it passes — and the click that follows opens it. That is conclusive.
- **"The panel is 250×149" was right**, and the cause was the inline style above, not a missing class.
  It now measures 384×460 in a 760×460 viewport, pinned to the right edge.

Neither was findable by reading the class list. **Read React Aria's own source for a component that
misbehaves** — `dist/private/<Name>.js.map` carries the original `tsx` in `sourcesContent`, which is how
the hardcoded `style` was found after two rounds of guessing.

## The root is `SheetTrigger`, not `DialogTrigger`

They take the same props and render the same element, and only one of them is right. React Aria's
`SheetTrigger` wraps its children in a `PressResponder` with `isPressed={false}`, in its own words to
_"prevent the trigger element from appearing stuck while the sheet is open"_. A plain `DialogTrigger`
leaves the button that opened the sheet looking pressed for as long as the sheet is up — which is exactly
what press-and-hold looks like, and is wrong.

It was found by reading React Aria's source rather than its types, because both are typed
`DialogTriggerProps` and the difference is one line of JSX.

## `SheetBackdrop` — attempted, measured, reverted

React Aria's animated scrim, which follows the panel out when a sheet is swiped. It was wired in, and the
attempt was reverted on evidence rather than on taste.

**The blocker is that React Aria owns the geometry of both layers.** A probe of the live DOM shows the
overlay reporting `position: absolute` where this component writes `fixed`, and the `Sheet` layer
reporting `relative` where it writes `absolute` — React Aria's own `sheetProps` set `position`, `top`,
`left`, `width` and `height` inline, and an inline style outranks every class. So the `Sheet` layer is
content-sized by the library, and `SheetBackdrop`'s `inset-0` can only ever resolve against **that** box.

The consequence is exact: a backdrop inside `Sheet` covers the **panel**, not the page. Making the layer
full-viewport is not a class away — it is React Aria's structure, and the first attempt collapsed the panel
from full-height to 149px, which the suite caught immediately.

The scrim therefore stays on the overlay, where it works and is tested.
